subject: Edge EIP translation: ephemeral port alignment causing connection drops
messages:
From: Samira Patel <ops@greenleaflabs.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: RiverNet Edge Support <edgeconnect@rivernet.io>
Date: Sun, 13 Dec 2026 16:22:00 -0800
Subject: Intermittent TLS failures to private deployment behind EIP

Hi Neha,

We started seeing intermittent TLS handshake failures from our app servers to the private deployment (Redwood private infra) after our recent outbound NAT gateway change. Symptoms: ~1-2% request failures (~500 errors) that correlate with a spike in TCP RSTs on the destination. Our ops team captured a pcap and a short VPC flowlog extract — attaching.

Notes:
- Traffic originates from a pool of app hosts in us-west-2 (ephemeral ports ~35000-61000).
- After replacing the NAT gateway with RiverNet-managed EIP translation, the connections that fail appear to have source ports remapped inconsistently during the session, which breaks session affinity on the Redwood front-door.
- We see successful flows when the source port is preserved end-to-end; failed flows show the EIP translation remapping mid-session.

Can you confirm whether Redwood's private edge supports hairpin / NAT reflection when clients are routing through the same public EIP, and whether there are any known cases where port remapping causes session drops?

Attaching: glab-eip-trace-20261213.pcap, vpc-flowlogs-snip-20261213.txt

Thanks,
Samira Patel
SRE Lead — GreenLeaf Labs
ops@greenleaflabs.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Patel <ops@greenleaflabs.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 13 Dec 2026 17:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent TLS failures to private deployment behind EIP

Hi Samira — thanks for the packet capture and the quick notes. I took a very quick look and looped in Rishi and Marissa from infra/networking and Laura from CS so we can coordinate with you.

Initial ask from our side: can you confirm whether the RiverNet EIP is performing any mid-flow port normalization / port preservation policy or a reverse-proxying step? If RiverNet is doing connection proxying rather than 1:1 SNAT, that could explain the mid-session port changes.

Rishi/Marissa: can you triage the following on our private edge side?
- Confirm whether our front-door accepts hairpinned connections from the same public IP (EIP) and preserves the original client ephemeral port.
- Check any recent SNAT table churn or port reuse thresholds that could cause the same source port to be remapped mid-session.
- Validate that our security group rules for the customer's private deployment allow the full ephemeral port range and don't rely on connection tracking for asymmetric behavior.

Samira — we will treat this as an escalation and keep you posted.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Samira Patel <ops@greenleaflabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 13 Dec 2026 18:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent TLS failures to private deployment behind EIP

Thanks — I pulled the pcap and flow logs. Quick read: I can see the SYN/ACK completing, then mid-long-lived connection we observe a second SYN from the client IP but different source port arriving at the backend (same 5-tuple not preserved). That strongly points to RiverNet doing a connection handoff / proxying layer where the source port is rewritten.

What I need from RiverNet:
- Clarify whether they run a layer that intentionally re-maps ephemeral ports for load balancing or connection multiplexing.
- If so, whether they support NAT reflection/hairpin so an incoming connection that exits via the same EIP retains the original client port.

On our side I'll check:
- Current conntrack table thresholds and SNAT port allocation policy on the private edge boxes (will provide output snapshot).
- Whether our front-door has a hairpin exemption (we do have a hairpin rule set historically but it may be bypassed for certain translation modes).

I'll attach a quick snapshot of our NAT table and conntrack counters in a follow-up. For now, two short mitigations we can try:
1) Add a temporary load-balancer rule to preserve client source port (if RiverNet supports passthrough mode).
2) Open a wider ephemeral port range on the customer security group to avoid blocked return flows while we diagnose port remapping.

-Rishi
Site Reliability Lead | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Samira Patel <ops@greenleaflabs.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 07:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent TLS failures to private deployment behind EIP

Quick analysis from the pcap (attached as glab-eip-trace-20261213.pcap) and a snapshot of our NAT rule file (edge-nat-rule-snapshot-20261213.txt):

Findings: 
- The client initiates from src port 42618; initial flow completes fine.
- Mid-session (long-lived websocket/TCP) RiverNet's translation shows a new flow originating from the same client IP but src port 40210 arriving at our backend. That map doesn't match conntrack expectations and results in the backend sending response to 40210 while the client's TCP stack still expects 42618, causing RSTs/handshake failures.
- Our current conntrack logs show ephemeral port exhaustion approaching threshold during the customer's morning traffic ramp (peak translation churn). We're seeing higher-than-normal SNAT port reuse rate which can cause collisions if an intermediate device reassigns ports.

Immediate remediation I recommend:
- As Rishi suggested, temporarily expand the security group allowed ephemeral range to 1024-65535 and increase conntrack port pool (we can do this for GreenLeaf's private tenant).
- Request RiverNet to enable port-preservation/passthrough for this specific EIP (we've done this previously for other clients).
- As a short-term workaround, schedule a brief maintenance window (5–10 minutes) to toggle a hairpin exemption on our edge routers to force 1:1 SNAT behavior for GreenLeaf's subnet.

Attachments included: vpc-flowlogs-snip-20261213.txt (from GreenLeaf), edge-nat-rule-snapshot-20261213.txt (our snapshot)

-Marissa
Network Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Patel <ops@greenleaflabs.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, RiverNet Edge Support <edgeconnect@rivernet.io>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent TLS failures to private deployment behind EIP

Samira — quick update and plan:

What we found:
- Root cause appears to be RiverNet's default translation layer performing connection handoffs that re-map ephemeral ports for long-lived flows. That, combined with elevated SNAT port reuse on our edge during the traffic ramp, led to mid-session port mismatches and the TLS failures you observed.

Action plan (short timeline):
1) Today 18:00 UTC: Marissa will increase conntrack port pool and toggle a hairpin exemption on the edge for GreenLeaf's subnet (expected 5m config window).
2) Today 19:00 UTC: RiverNet to attempt a passthrough/port-preservation setting for the EIP (RiverNet confirmed they can try this in a configurable manner).
3) We will keep the security group ephemeral range opened temporarily and monitor. If no regressions after 24h, we'll tighten SG rules and remove the temporary conntrack bump.

Laura from CS will coordinate the customer maintenance window with you and share monitoring links.

Samira — could you confirm a preferred 1h window tonight for the two short ops actions and the best Slack channel to use for play-by-play?

Thanks all — will follow up with the config diffs once Marissa has applied them.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
